    `vteam_` (platform-tool-permission.service.ts:44) → maps to `secret.command`
    via capabilityKeyForTool('vteam_secret_command') (coverage spec:61) → allowlist key

3.2 ERROR PATHS — PASS
  worker route exec-server.ts:1328-1412: 405 (non-POST) → 401 (missing/wrong/unset token,
    log carries no token value) → 413 (readBody + drainRequest) → 400 (bad JSON / non-object /
    missing requestId) → 409 (same requestId, different taskId/sessionId) → replay of the
    SAME promise for concurrent duplicates (record registered at exec-server.ts:1393-1399
    BEFORE any await)
    → `executeSecretCommand` NEVER rejects: SensitiveCommandError → fixed 400 string per code
    table (SECRET_COMMAND_REJECTIONS, exec-server.ts:341); any other throwable → fixed
    `'internal error'` 500 with `err.message` deliberately NOT echoed (1435-1466).
  server handler platform-mcp.service.ts:4224-4384: order 400 validate → 403 ownership →
    403 managed fail-closed BEFORE createSecretForPlatform (no orphan pending row) → 503
    missing worker row → 403 no session → 409 in-flight → `finally` always
    clearInterval + Set.delete (4380-4383) → worker failure normalised by
    toSecretCommandError (4580) with secret-exact redaction of every foreign message.
  abort/timeout: input budget timer (540s) and AbortSignal listener are attached with
    `once` + removed in `finally` (awaitSecretInput 4499-4564); non-hook outcome cancels the
    still-pending question through the `{secrets:null}` bypass (cancelSecretQuestion 4566)
    so no ghost execution can survive an MCP disconnect/expiry. A second guard re-checks
    `signal?.aborted` after the value arrives and before dispatch (4336).
  questions: missing `secrets` → 400, undeclared key → 400, declared-but-missing value →

    class-validator CONDITIONAL_VALIDATION, so null skips `@IsObject()` (verified in
    class-validator 0.14.4 ValidationExecutor.performValidations:135-151); cancel is not
    broken by the ValidationPipe.

3.5 THE DISCLOSED FIRST-TOKEN EXEMPTION (worker/src/driver/prompt-await.ts) — ASSESSMENT
  What changed (the whole product delta of todo 9 is +36/−1 lines):
    :388-394  IN_FLIGHT_TOOL_STATES = new Set(['pending','running'])   ← tool-AGNOSTIC whitelist
    :396-416  hasInFlightTool(messages) — assistant tool parts only; `state` must be an object
              and `status` a string in the whitelist; unknown/missing status ⇒ NO exemption.
    :563      the single behavioural edit:
              `… && firstTokenAt === null && !hasInFlightTool(collected) && Date.now()-… >= firstTokenTimeoutMs`
              i.e. the exemption can only suppress the FIRST-TOKEN abort; it does not touch
              finish detection, info.error early-fail (518), serve-log early-fail (528),
              activity-signature extension (556-560), or any post-first-token behaviour.

  Is “tool-agnostic {pending,running}” appropriately bounded?
    Worker side: NOT time-bounded (that is the disclosed gap — there is no timer in the
    exempt branch; while ANY tool part stays pending/running the 300s first-token clock is
    suspended). Bound comes from the server, in three layers, tightest first:
      (a) motivating case secret_command — its own budget caps the exemption:
          SECRET_INPUT_BUDGET_MS 540s (questions.constants.ts:45) + timeoutSec ≤300s
          + SECRET_COMMAND_REQUEST_SLACK_MS 5s = ≤845s < VTEAM_MCP_TIMEOUT_FLOOR_MS 900000
          (injector.ts:146, clamped Math.max(parsed, floor) at :163). The tool part MUST
          reach a terminal status inside that window; the moment it does, the exemption is
          gone and a still-absent first token aborts at 300s from lastActivityAt.
          keepAliveSession only runs while this bounded wait/execute is in flight and is
          always cleared in `finally` (platform-mcp.service.ts:4301 / 4380-4383), so the
          plan's own code can never keep the exemption alive indefinitely.
      (b) any OTHER tool stuck pending/running — server silent watchdog:
          DEFAULT_SILENT_SESSION_WAKE_MS = 600_000 (worker-dispatcher.ts:766), sliding,
          ×MAX_SILENT_WAKE_ATTEMPTS then the failure path (silent_session_timeout).
      (c) the cited 30-minute fallback — DEFAULT_AGENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 30 * 60_000
          (worker-dispatcher.ts:777, env AGENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS): scanIdleSessions (4646)
          → markSessionIdleDead (4722) sets status=failed, clears the watchdog and
          best-effort calls abortStuckWorkerSession (4803-4807 → workerClient.abort), which
          is what actually terminates the worker's polling loop.
      caveat (recorded, not a defect): markSessionIdleDead has a memory veto — a session
      still registered in isAgentExecuting is skipped (4742-4755, 30-min TTL), so (c) can be
      deferred by up to that TTL; (b) still fires first on a genuinely silent session, and
      keepAliveSession never runs outside the secret budget, so the fallback cannot be
      pushed out indefinitely by plan code.
    Verdict: the exemption is real, deliberately tool-agnostic, whitelist-bounded (not
    blacklist), and closed by pre-existing server watchdogs; for the feature that motivated
    it the tight bound is 855s, not 30 minutes. ACCEPTED as disclosed.
    Documentation status: documented in code (JSDoc 388-394 and 479-481) and in
    task-9-integration.txt §6 (explicit `>> DEVIATION（必须记录）` block with 3 red-on-old
    tests and QA-B reverse proof) and acknowledged by F1 (final-f1-plan-compliance.txt D2,
    which hands this exact question to F2). NOT documented in
    docs/secret-command-tool.md — the operator doc covers budgets/keepalive/orphans but is
    silent on the suspended first-token window (doc-only gap → Q7).

4. FINDINGS (file:line, severity) — none blocks APPROVE
==============================================================================
Q1  MINOR / P3 — placeholder whitespace contract mismatch.
    server/src/platform-mcp/platform-mcp.service.ts:351-356 uses /\{\{\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\}\}/g
    and its comment + docs/secret-command-tool.md §6 both promise "`{{ name }}` 带空格亦识别";
    worker/src/exec/sensitive-command.ts:40-41 SUBSTITUTE_RE / PLACEHOLDER_RE have NO \s.
    Effect: a spaced placeholder passes server validation (and is even required to be
    declared) but is never substituted and never masked on the worker — the command runs
    with literal `{{ NAME }}`. No secret leaks (the value simply never reaches the command),
    but the call silently does the wrong thing and the literal placeholder can appear in
    model-visible output. No test covers spaced placeholders. Suggest aligning the worker
    regex or narrowing the server/doc claim.
Q2  MINOR / P3 — server-side re-truncation ignores UTF-8 boundaries.
    platform-mcp.service.ts:4630+ `scrub()` does bytes.subarray(0, 32768) without the
    boundary back-off that worker cutBytes (sensitive-command.ts:232-241) performs. Only
    reachable when redaction EXPANDS an already worker-truncated stream (short secrets →
    `***` longer than the value): possible trailing U+FFFD. Cosmetic.
Q3  MINOR / P3 — response cast instead of enum validation.
    worker.client.ts runSecretCommand validates only `typeof result.status === 'string'`
    then casts to SecretCommandResult; an unexpected status string would flow into
    SecretCommandEnvelope.status. Source is the local worker, whose toSecretCommandResponse
    picks fields explicitly and is pinned by contract.spec.ts, so risk is low — an
    `includes(status)` guard would make the narrowing total.
Q4  MINOR / ACCEPTED (documented) — abort is only checked BEFORE dispatch.
    platform-mcp.service.ts:4336; once runSecretCommand is in flight an MCP disconnect does
    not cancel the worker command (server keeps its own HTTP connection open). Disclosed in
    docs/secret-command-tool.md §8「执行已下发后取消不追回」; bounded by ≤300s command
    timeout + 5s. Correct per plan wording (“在这之前超时/断开”).
Q5  INFO — child inherits the full worker environment (`env: process.env`,
    sensitive-command.ts:327). No sandbox by plan scope; disclosed as docs §5.2. A secret
    never enters process.env (values travel only in the request body), so this does not
    widen the secret surface.
Q6  INFO / P4 — ordering micro-nit: the keepalive interval and the in-flight Set insert are
    created at platform-mcp.service.ts:4299-4303 but the `try` opens only at :4308; a throw
    from `this.logger.log(...)` in between would leak the timer/Set. pino does not throw in
    practice; not worth a change inside F2.
Q7  DOC-ONLY — the first-token exemption (§3.5) is not mentioned in
    docs/secret-command-tool.md §8 (operator/ops view), although code JSDoc + task-9 §6 +
    F1 D2 document it. Suggest one sentence: “在途工具 pending/running 会挂起 worker 300s
    首字判定，兜底为 server 静默看门狗 600s×N 与 AGENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=30min（含 worker abort）”.

Positive (verified, no finding): enqueue/queue discipline in web (questionQueue dedupe by id,
reset on `questionId` change so a queued-in secret never lands in the next modal —
question-modal.tsx:143-147), cancel-on-close emits `{secrets:null}` from ONE shared entry
point (buildSecretReply), awaiting-input derivation is data-driven from pending secret_input
questions (page.tsx:516-541, msg-parts.tsx:115 + :198) and self-clears on tool terminal state,
idempotency cache bounded with settled-only eviction (exec-server.ts:368, 1418-1433),
MCP timeout floor clamped (injector.ts:152-164, applied at :693).

3. CODE-QUALITY REVIEW OF THE THREE REMEDIATION CHANGES

3.1  todo 11 — que requestId resync (commit a30397e)                    [APPROVE]
     files: server/src/common/id-resync.ts, id-resync.spec.ts,
            id-resync.guard.spec.ts, questions.service.ts,
            questions.service.spec.ts

  + Design: new `resyncRequestIdPrefix(model, idPrefix, requestIdPrefix, idGen)`
    mirrors the existing `resyncIdPrefix`; the P2021 fail-open background retry
    was extracted into a shared `startP2021Retry()` so both paths keep the exact
    pre-existing behaviour (non-P2021 still throws; P2021 never blocks
    `onModuleInit`). Refactor is behaviour-preserving for the old path — proven
    by the unchanged guard spec and the full green `src/common` suite.
  + Correctness of parsing: rows are re-filtered against `que_platform_` (so
    `per_…`/`que_…` rows can't pollute), non-numeric tails, empty tails and
    > Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER tails are skipped, and `seed()` is only called when
    `max > 0`. Tail `0000000007` → `seed('que', 7)` → next `que_platform_0000000008`.
  + Scope fidelity: no change to the `@unique` constraint, no change to the
    `que_platform_` format, no new dependency, no schema/migration.
  + Test quality (RED-first, verified green):
      – id-resync.spec: asserts the *query shape* (`where.requestId.startsWith
        'que_platform_'` + `select.requestId`) so "didn't query but still green"
        is impossible; 7→8 continuation; junk/oversized/foreign rows ignored;
        empty table → starts at 1; P2021 resolves undefined (fail-open);
        non-P2021 rejects. 6 new cases.
      – questions.service.spec: builds a *fresh* `IdGeneratorService` (simulating
        restart), seeds `findMany` with `que_platform_0000000007`, then asserts the
        **persisted** `data.requestId` is `que_platform_0000000008` and the second
        create `…09` — i.e. it asserts the DB write, not just `seed()`. Exactly the
        plan's acceptance wording.
  + Guard spec: `que` removed from `RESYNC_EXEMPT` with the corrected rationale
    (request_id is `@unique`, not "no constraint at all") and the prefix-scanner
    now recognises both `resyncIdPrefix(` and `resyncRequestIdPrefix(` — removing
    the new call would turn this source-scanning guard RED.
  + Type safety: `ResyncRequestIdModel.findMany` returns `Promise<unknown>` with
    explicit casts, deliberately mirroring `ResyncIdModel`; `tsc` (gate build,
    `lint:check`) clean.
  – Note (non-blocking, pre-existing behaviour kept): the shared P2021 background
    retry increments attempts on *any* retry error, not only P2021 — identical to
    the pre-refactor code, so not a regression introduced here (Q7).

3.2  todo 12 — team-scope create emit + matchesScope fallback (commit 1b31521)   [APPROVE]
     files: server/src/questions/questions.service.ts (+spec),
            web/hooks/use-sse.ts, web/hooks/use-sse.scope.test.mjs,
            web/e2e/session-unification.spec.ts

  + Server: `scopeOf(row.taskId, row.sessionId)` is hoisted into `createScope` /
    `secretScope` and reused for both the new top-level `teamId` field and the
    emit scope — one lookup, same call count as before, so no ordering or extra
    query change (resolvers are still registered before emit).
  + `teamId: scope.type === 'team' ? scope.id : null` ⇒ task/global/channel scoped
    emits carry `null`, which can never equal a `team:<id>` scope string, so the
    fallback **cannot** widen matching to another team (no cross-team leak).
    `payload.taskId` is untouched ⇒ task-scope consumers and existing page guards
    keep working (additive field only).
  + Web: exactly one clause added, in the `team:` branch only:
      `|| (ev.payload as {teamId?: string})?.teamId === id`
    `channel:`/`global:`/`task:` branches unchanged; an absent `teamId` still
    returns false (explicitly tested).
  + Tests: server spec now asserts `teamId: 'tm_1'` on BOTH `createForPlatform`
    and `createSecretForPlatform` emits; `use-sse.scope.test.mjs` gains the three
    production-shape cases required by the plan (match / other-team drop /
    missing-teamId drop) — all 45 tests green (T6). An e2e production-shape

3.3  todo 13 — MCP blocking-call heartbeat (commit 0987980)             [APPROVE]
     files: server/src/platform-mcp/platform-mcp.controller.ts (+spec)

  + Opt-in gate: `acceptsEventStream(req)` splits `Accept` on `,` and matches the
    media type `text/event-stream` exactly (parameters stripped). opencode 1.18.32
    sends `application/json, text/event-stream` ⇒ SSE path; curl's default `*/*`
    never matches ⇒ the response stays one plain JSON document via `res.json(out)`.
    Both shapes are covered by dedicated spec cases.
  + Budget: `MCP_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000` ≤ the plan's 60s ceiling, so any
    60s scan window sees ≥2 bytes-carrying frames. Frames are SSE comments
    (`: vteam-mcp-heartbeat <ts>\n\n`) which are ignored by SSE parsers and do not
    interfere with the final `data:` JSON-RPC frame.
  + Headers only flip on the FIRST heartbeat ⇒ fast returns (non-promise dispatch,
    or an event-stream client resolving <30s) keep the original single-JSON-body
    contract — spec case "快速返回（非阻塞）" asserts no `setHeader`/`write` and a
    plain `res.json(...)` result.
  + Final frame is a legal JSON-RPC message: `endWithJsonRpcFrame` writes one
    `data: {jsonrpc, id, result|error}` frame and `res.end()`; the spec
    `JSON.parse`s it and asserts `jsonrpc:'2.0'`, `id:91`, and the parsed tool
    payload. Errors that occur AFTER takeover are re-framed as
    `error(id, -32603, …)` with the original request id (via `messageId(body)`);
    errors BEFORE takeover rethrow to the Nest exception path exactly as before.
  + Disconnect semantics unchanged and audited: `res.on('close')` +
    `req.on('aborted')` are registered BEFORE dispatch and still abort
    `disconnect.signal`; the spec asserts `signal.aborted === true` after `close`
    and that no further heartbeat/`end()` write happens afterwards.
  + Timer hygiene: `clearInterval` in `finally`, plus `res.on('close', stop)` with
    a matching `res.off('close', stop)`, plus `timer.unref()` ⇒ no timer survives
    settle or disconnect, no listener leak across requests.
  + `@Res({ passthrough: true })` → raw `@Res()`: verified this cannot silently
    drop/re-wrap bodies — `grep useGlobalInterceptors|APP_INTERCEPTOR server/src`
    returns NOTHING, `server/src/main.ts` only calls `useGlobalPipes`, and no other
    `passthrough` remains in the controller; the GET/405 handler still returns its
    value to Nest untouched. Notification path still returns `{accepted:true}` with
    HTTP 202 (dispatch returns it synchronously ⇒ `res.status(202)` + `res.json`).
  + Must-NOTs: no MCP method/event name change (`grep` shows none), no server-side
    global timeout added, curl/JSON parsing preserved (explicit spec), and the
    `secret_command` wait/keepalive contract is untouched.
  + Tests: 4 new fake-timer cases, all green inside T1 —
      (a) SSE client: exactly `[2,2,2,2,2,2]` writes per 60s window (30s cadence),
          SSE response headers set, every write matches the comment regex, final
          frame parseable, `res.json` NOT called;
      (b) `*/*` client: 600s advanced with ZERO writes/setHeader, plain JSON body;
      (c) disconnect: signal aborts, then 600s more ⇒ still 1 write, no `end()`;
      (d) fast path: no heartbeat, plain JSON body.
